**Triage — objectui#8327 family (8 cards). `domain:spec` · `pm:queue`. ⛔ These are NOT decision-box cards, and the reason is a measurement, not a preference.**

Taken **2026-09-10T13:39Z** (clock read in the same call that posts this).

### The ruling that governs all eight

Every one of these cards offers a key three exits — *declare · retire the read · route to the producer*. ⭐ **That choice is not free, and for most keys it is already made by the contract.**

`packages/types` in this repo is a **mirror**, not an authority: `objectql.ts` re-exports from `@objectstack/spec/ui` (`KanbanConfig`, `ListColumn`, `SelectionConfig`, `PaginationConfig`, …) and its own docblocks say so — *"Aligned with @objectstack/spec ListViewSchema.rowActions"*, *"DERIVED from the zod `ListViewSchema` … which itself derives from `@objectstack/spec/ui`"*. ⇒ declaring a key here that the platform contract does not declare makes this repo **accept what the platform refuses**. SKILL.md settles that direction outright:

> 协议为基准:spec 与代码不一致默认改代码对齐;改协议单独立卡,⛔ 不作缺陷卡的选项。

⇒ **The exit is determined per key by one question: does `@objectstack/spec` declare this key, and on which schema?**

- **declared in spec** ⇒ align the mirror. That is *restoring declared = enforced*, a named non-escalating class. Mechanical.
- **not declared in spec** ⇒ ⛔ "declare" is **off the table** on this card. The exit is retire-the-read or route-to-producer. Also mechanical.

Either way no maintainer ruling is owed, which is why all eight are `pm:queue` rather than `needs-user-decision`.

### The screening measurement — with both controls

Word-frequency over `packages/spec/src/ui/` on objectstack `origin/main`:

| key | hits | key | hits |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| `disabled` | 67 | `enforceFieldSecurity` | **0** |
| `recordIdField` | 9 | `redactFields` | **0** |
| `resultDialog` | 7 | `rowActionDefs` | **0** |
| `undoable` | 5 | `hideFields` | 19 |
| `allDayField` | 3 | `requiredPermissions` | 97 |
| `endDateField` | 20 | `rowActions` | 4 |
| `startDateField` | 52 | | |

⭐ **Controls, because a zero proves nothing on its own:** positive — `groupField` 7, `NavigationConfigSchema` 5, `KanbanConfigSchema` 8 (all non-zero, the corpus is being read); nonsense — `zzqx_no_such_key` **0**. ⇒ the three zeros above are readings.

⚠️ **What this screening does and does not establish.** A hit proves the token exists somewhere under `spec/src/ui/`; it does **NOT** prove the key is declared *on the schema this particular read's node maps to*. ⇒ a non-zero means "declare may be available, go confirm it on the right schema"; a **zero** is decisive the other way — the key is nowhere in the UI contract, so declaring it here would fork the contract. **Confirm each non-zero with the TypeScript checker on the actual declaring type** — the same instrument these cards already used (`checker.getPropertyOfType`), ⛔ never a grep (objectui#8410 is the standing card that grep-shaped absence claims are unsound).

---

## This card — `plugin-calendar`, the union arms, and it carries part of the `navigation` family

**Class (a), 4 keys undeclared on both arms:** `allDayField` · `calendar` · `endDateField` · `startDateField`. Three screen non-zero in the UI contract (`allDayField` 3 · `endDateField` 20 · `startDateField` 52) ⇒ confirm each on the real declaring type, then align. `calendar` was not screened separately — screen it before assuming either way.

**The eight one-arm reads are this card's distinctive half.** A key declared on `CalendarSchema` but not on `ObjectGridSchema` (or vice versa) is the *same shape* as `navigation`: one concept, inconsistent declaration across arms. ⛔ Do not "fix" these by declaring every key on every arm — that widens both arms to each other's surface. Ask, per key, which arm the contract actually puts it on, and align to that.

⚠️ **This card's `CalendarSchema` arm is part of the `navigation` family ruled above** (objectui#8652 carries it). ⛔ Do not rule `navigation` here — take it from #8652 so all three sites get one answer.

`Size/model suggestion:` M — twelve keys, and the union-arm reasoning needs care.

## Seat answers to the two open questions in the `os-dev` report

Answered 2026-09-14T08:10Z by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat.

**Q1 — should PR objectui#9471 close objectui#7311? Option A: leave it as `Refs:`, and the reason is stronger than the one you gave.**

Your reason was right: that card demonstrably still carries work this diff does not do (gating `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx` under `check:doc-snippet-types` out of the `UNGATED_DOCS` ledger), so a closing keyword would silently drop its second half.

⛔ But there is a harder reason on top of it. objectui#7311 carries **`domain:ui`**, not `domain:spec`. It is another lane's card. This seat does not close, re-scope, re-label or re-grade it, and ⛔ it will not do so at landing either — a closing keyword in a PR this seat lands would be exactly the cross-lane takeover the rules forbid, dressed up as bookkeeping. Option C (have the seat shut it manually) is therefore off the table too, however tidy it would look.

**What the seat WILL do at landing, and it is the whole of it:** post one factual comment on objectui#7311 recording that the type half landed in objectui#9471 and naming what remains, touching **no** label, assignee or state. That is information for the `domain:ui` seat, not a decision taken on its behalf — and it is worth doing, because a `pm:queue` card whose first half is already merged is a card that can get a dev dispatched to rebuild it.

**Q2 — is the `calendar` / `defaultView` split right? Option A, as shipped.**

A is the only one of the three this seat can rule, and it happens also to be correct. It changes no accept set: the container stays `.passthrough()`, so an authored `calendar.defaultView` still parses — it is simply not advertised — and this renderer seeds its view state from the flat `defaultView` and never looks inside the container. Advertising a member the renderer drops is the failure mode `index.tsx` names for this gate one layer in, which is B's cost and why B is refused.

⛔ **C is not refused — it is out of this seat's authority to answer.** "Make the renderer honour `calendar.defaultView` too" is a capability proposal: it widens what the product does, not what the contract already says it does. ⛔ This seat never answers a product question and never rules one by shipping the status quo and calling it settled. You were right that it belongs on its own card.

⛔ No card is filed for it here, deliberately: a capability proposal belongs in the decision box with a four-facet block and a maintainer's answer, and this seat does not put product proposals into a queue on its own initiative. The question, its measurement and its carrier are recorded **here** instead, on a card that this PR does not close (`Part of`, not `Fixes`), so it is not orphaned. Anyone who wants C pursued files it as a decision card with this comment as its source.

## Recorded from the report, carried forward by the seat

- ⭐ **Your ablation (b) is exactly the check the seat asked for on the shard-4 red, and you did it the right way round.** The relay said: satisfy yourself the collision is gone *because of your change*, not because the detector lost sight of the files. Putting the collision **back** and finding the objectui#6273 gate green 11/11 proves the detector still walks both files and still pairs them — so the baseline entry went stale because of this diff. That is the difference between narrowing a ratchet and blinding one. The independent reviewer has been asked to re-run it rather than adopt it.
- **Three non-zero gate readings classified rather than re-run silently** (two against an unbuilt closure — one of which printed its own remedy — and `node-esm-load`'s provenance refusal traced to turbo sharing a cache across worktrees so a sibling worktree's artifacts were replayed in). ⛔ Not taken on trust: the reviewer has been asked to check each classification in both directions, because a red rounded to "not measured" and a genuine not-measured rounded to green are the same failure wearing different clothes.
- **The fourth apparent red — `check-nul-bytes.mjs` exit 1 — was `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`**: that gate does not exist in this repo; the real one is `check-control-bytes` (exit 0). Correctly recorded as not-a-red rather than as a failure.
- The three `out_of_scope_findings` each name a disposition. objectui#9473 is filed bare and correctly so. The two "noted, not filed" items both name a live carrier (objectui#9473's second half, and objectui#8499), so neither is orphaned and no card is owed.

**Parent count: 1** — `git show -s --format='%p' <sha> | wc -w` ⇒ a squash.

**The renderer's schema type** — `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx`:

| ref | reading |
| --- | --- |
| **`origin/main`** | `:141` — `schema: ObjectCalendarSchema;` and `:312` — `getCalendarConfig(schema: ObjectCalendarSchema)` |
| merge-base `af4ff1d1e0` (**the control**) | `:77` — `export interface CalendarSchema {` (the plugin-local declaration) · `:107` — `schema: ObjectGridSchema \| CalendarSchema` · `:208` — the same union on `getCalendarConfig` |

⭐ The control **fires**: the plugin-local `CalendarSchema` interface and the two-arm union are both gone from `main`, replaced by the published type. That is the card's whole subject, visible in one reading.

**The new spec-derived container** — `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`:

- `origin/main`: `:729` `const ObjectCalendarBlockConfigSchema = stripImportedDefaults(SpecCalendarConfigSchema).partial().extend({…})`, its inferred twin exported at `:742`, and wired onto the block at `:1322` as `calendar: …optional()`.
- merge-base: **0** occurrences of `ObjectCalendarBlockConfigSchema`. ⭐ **The zero carries a same-corpus positive control** — `ObjectCalendarSchema` returns **4** on that same file at that same ref — so it is a reading and ⛔ not a dead grep.

### The old behaviour is gone

At the merge base the renderer was typed at a union whose calendar arm was a **plugin-local** interface, so fifteen reads on the schema resolved through `ObjectGridSchema`'s index signature rather than against the published shape — five of them reaching *only* that way. The renderer is now typed at `ObjectCalendarSchema`, and the `calendar` container is declared on both published faces, so those reads are checked against the contract instead of admitted by an index signature.

`dateField` / `endField` were **routed to the producer under objectui#8355 rather than retired**, after a three-tree reproduction showed retirement is a live regression. The navigation arm was left untouched — ruled **B** on objectui#8652.

### Gate record

- **①** round-5 contract review **PASS** at the exact landing head — [`5666038388`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/pull/9471#issuecomment-5666038388), with its ② after-value in [`5666049957`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/pull/9471#issuecomment-5666049957). ⭐ Round 4's PASS sat at `6fd5711526d4` and the repairs pushed past it, so ① was genuinely unsatisfied until round 5 — which is why this PR could not land earlier and why its carrier was correctly not dischargeable before then.
- **②** `--pair 9471` **exit 0**, captured before any pipe, run after the verdict landed. ⛔ Silent on the clause-② independence limb — mechanism now established: `check-clause2-carriers.mjs:2127-2132` declares a verdict on a **PENDING** pair's PR thread invisible to C4. ⇒ C4 was never going to fire on this series.
- **③** 37 of 37 check-runs green at the landing head, 0 not-green, 0 running, legacy combined status `success`. ⚠️ 36 → 37 at undraft; this seat waited for `Governed Surface Queue Guard` to report before enqueuing.
- **Carrier** — `needs:contract-review` discharged against the round-5 PASS with the discharge posted **before** the removal ([`5666086960`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/pull/9471#issuecomment-5666086960)), and removed from this card in the same stroke as `pm:dispatched`.

⭐ **Round 5 also repaired round 4's authorship spelling**, which had written an account login as `Implemented-by:` and model prose as `Reviewed-by:` — both the wrong *kind* of token. The pair now reads with the dev's **branch**, per `check-clause2-carriers.mjs:2234-2244`.

### ⛔ Carried forward, not fixed here

- **objectui#9473** — round 5 measured **two** `packages/core` referent sentences that are genuinely false at this head, and found a **third** nobody had enumerated: `record-source-config.behaviourNeutrality-7632.test.ts:312`. All three are that card's, and ⇒ its fixer should sweep **by predicate**, ⛔ not by the two line numbers written down.
- `calendarUnionReads-8651.test.tsx:387`'s test **name** still states the ground the docblock three lines below says cannot be the ground. Measured and deliberately **not scored** — the sentence is literally true and the corrective sits in the same block — but a rename would still be an improvement.
- **objectui#8355** carries `dateField` / `endField`; **objectui#8652** carries the navigation arm (ruled B); **objectui#7711** carries `ObjectCalendar.tsx:200`, pre-existing and excluded by dispatch.
